papers.title: Brain-Gut Axis Perspective on Irritable Bowel Syndrome: The Role of Gut Microbiota and Therapeutic Strategies of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.journal: The American journal of Chinese medicine
papers.authors: Yu A, Bi Y, Xu X
papers.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is one of the most common functional gastrointestinal disorders, with dysfunction of the gut-brain axis (GBA) being its core pathogenic mechanism. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), guided by the theory of "liver-spleen interaction" and the core therapeutic principle of "soothing the liver and invigorating the spleen", has accumulated extensive clinical experience in IBS treatment. This review systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, and CNKI databases to summarize the molecular mechanisms by which gut microbiota participate in IBS pathogenesis through the GBA, interpret the modern biological connotation of the TCM pathogenesis of "liver depression and spleen deficiency" from the perspective of the GBA, and review the evidence for TCM in treating IBS by modulating gut microbiota. The results indicate that gut microbiota dysbiosis drives IBS symptoms through three major metabolic pathways - short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and 5-hydroxytryptamine - and achieves bidirectional regulation via the GBA. TCM monomers (e.g., berberine, curcumin, apigenin), single herbs (e.g., Atractylodes, Cinnamomum, Liupao tea), classical formulas (e.g., Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang, Chang-Kang-Fang, Si-Ni-San), as well as acupuncture and moxibustion, may improve IBS symptoms by restoring gut microbial diversity, regulating metabolite levels, repairing the intestinal barrier, and inhibiting inflammatory pathways. TCM may offer unique advantages in treating IBS through multi-target regulation of gut microbiota. Future research should focus on the objectification of TCM syndrome differentiation based on gut microbiota and the development of precision matching strategies.

papers.title: Curcumin from Turmeric Alleviates Lipid Metabolism: Network Pharmacology and Cellular Validation.
papers.journal: The American journal of Chinese medicine
papers.authors: Niu LS, Zhang YZ, Wu FY, Qi WH, Ren C, Xu YS et al.
papers.abstract: Curcumin, the primary active compound in turmeric, a widely used medicinal and edible herb in traditional Chinese medicine, exhibits beneficial effects against lipid metabolic dysfunction (LMD). Nevertheless, its comprehensive regulatory network and precise mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vitro cellular assays were integrated to elucidate the targets and mechanisms by which curcumin acts against LMD. Seven hub targets were identified: AKT1, ALB, INS, IL6, TP53, TNF, and PPARG. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analysis revealed significant enrichment of these hub targets in multiple pathways, with a notable emphasis on non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. Molecular docking confirmed that curcumin exhibited a favorable binding affinity to the hub targets. Cellular experiments using oleic acid-induced human hepatocellular carcinoma HepG2 cells demonstrated that curcumin markedly reduced triglyceride and total cholesterol levels, alleviated lipid droplet accumulation, and significantly modulated the mRNA expression of genes involved in lipid metabolism, anti-oxidant defense, and inflammation. These findings were consistent with predictions from network pharmacology. In summary, curcumin may alleviate OA-induced LMD by synergistically modulating lipid metabolism, inhibiting oxidative damage, and diminishing inflammation. This study provides a comprehensive theoretical basis for the application of curcumin in LMD intervention.

papers.title: Effect of SFMA-guided Qihuang Needling vs conventional acupuncture on paraspinal neuromuscular activity in lumbar disc herniation: A randomised controlled trial.
papers.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
papers.authors: Yuan S, Liu H, Huang Y, Zeng J, Deng W, Peng Z et al.
papers.abstract: BackgroundLumbar disc herniation (LDH) commonly causes chronic low back and leg pain. Qihuang Needling (QN) is a micro-invasive technique targeting myofascial dysfunction, but its effects on paraspinal neuromuscular activity have not been objectively quantified.ObjectiveTo determine whether SFMA-guided QN produces greater immediate improvement than conventional acupuncture (CA) in paraspinal neuromuscular activity.MethodsIn this single-centre, assessor- and statistician-blinded trial, 68 outpatients with LDH were allocated 1:1 to five daily sessions of SFMA-guided QN or CA. The primary endpoint was static multifidus AEMG, analysed by ANCOVA with baseline adjustment; pain and disability were exploratory endpoints.ResultsAll 68 participants completed the trial. Static multifidus AEMG increased more with QN than CA (adjusted difference 7.43 μV, 95% CI 2.74 to 12.12; P = 0.002). All seven secondary sEMG endpoints also improved more with QN after false-discovery-rate control. The Oswestry Disability Index difference was -17.17 points (95% CI -20.53 to -13.81); responder rates were 76.5% versus 35.3% (P = 0.001). No serious adverse events occurred.ConclusionsFive daily sessions of SFMA-guided QN produced greater immediate improvement in paraspinal neuromuscular activity than CA. Whether these differences persist, and which components account for them, cannot be determined from this trial.

papers.title: Effects of Acupuncture at ST36 and SP6 on Activity Levels and Pain Thresholds Through Interleukin-1, Interleukin-6, Cortisol, and Matrix Metalloproteinase-13 Modulation in an Osteoarthritis Rat Model.
papers.authors: Wulandari M, Handono K, Khotimah H, Yuliatun L
papers.abstract:
Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage degradation, inflammation, and altered stress-related responses. This preclinical study examined the effects of acupuncture at ST36 (stomach 36), SP6 (spleen 6), and their combination on pain thresholds, locomotor function, and inflammation and stress-related biomarkers in a monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced OA rat model.
Thirty male Wistar rats were randomized into five groups a healthy control, an OA control, and three acupuncture-treated groups (ST36, SP6, and ST36 + SP6). Acupuncture-treated groups underwent eight 15-min sessions of acupuncture per day. Pain thresholds and locomotor activity were assessed before and after treatment. Joint tissue was analyzed for interleukin (IL)-1, IL-6, cortisol, and matrix metalloproteinase-13 (MMP-13) levels. Group differences were analyzed using appropriate parametric or nonparametric tests, and the associations between biomarkers and behavioral outcomes were assessed using Pearson correlation analysis.
The acupuncture-treated rats showed increased pain thresholds (~5.3 g to 9.93-11.60 g, p < 0.05) and higher locomotor activity compared with those in the OA controls. IL-1, IL-6, cortisol, and MMP-13 levels were reduced from pretreatment levels in all acupuncture groups. Biomarker levels were negatively correlated with pain thresholds (r = -0.526 to -0.686) and locomotor activity (r = -0.537 to -0.893; all p < 0.01).
In rats with MIA-induced OA, acupuncture was associated with improved pain thresholds and locomotor outcomes and changes in inflammation and stress-related biomarker levels, providing exploratory preclinical evidence linking biomarker modulation with functional responses.

papers.title: Herbal and Natural Products for NSAID-Induced Small Intestinal Injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.authors: Hwang JH, Choi YK
papers.abstract:
Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), including aspirin, are widely used medications that frequently cause small intestinal injury (enteropathy). Conventional proton pump inhibitors do not prevent this injury and may exacerbate it through dysbiosis. Herbal medicines and natural products offer potential therapeutic benefits, but synthesized clinical evidence remains limited. Thus, this study will systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of herbal medicines and natural products for preventing NSAID-induced small intestinal injury.
MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure will be searched to identify articles published since inception, without restrictions on publication date or language. Randomized controlled trials involving adults aged ≥ 18 years receiving NSAIDs will be included. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using the RoB 2 tool. If appropriate, a meta-analysis will be conducted. The primary outcome will be mucosal injury, objectively assessed using video capsule endoscopy or measures of intestinal permeability. Secondary outcomes will include symptoms and adverse events.
This study will synthesize the current clinical evidence on natural interventions for NSAID-induced enteropathy.
The findings will inform the management of small intestinal injury and guide future research.

papers.title: Source-Audited Mining and Visualization of Real-World Traditional Chinese Medicine Case Records Using Hegan Jianpi Formula.
papers.authors: Xia T, Zhang R, Gu Y, Tian Z, Zheng Z, Chu X et al.
papers.abstract: Real-world traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) outpatient records contain longitudinal information on diagnoses, syndrome elements, symptom narratives, and individualized prescriptions, but their semi-structured format complicates reproducible analysis. This article presents a source-audited protocol for converting de-identified case records into traceable aggregate tables and publication-ready visualizations. The workflow defines eligibility criteria and analysis units, preserves mappings between original and normalized terminology, verifies all reported numerators and denominators, and regenerates figures from versioned source tables. Applied to records from January 2015 through June 2024, the protocol identified 555 eligible prescription visits from 396 patients. The final dataset contained 324 normalized herb labels and 9,339 herb-use occurrences. The workflow generated parallel Western medicine and TCM disease spectra, an explicit syndrome-element spectrum and co-occurrence matrix, herb-frequency and materia medica profiles, a 37-term history-derived symptom spectrum, 15 directed association rules, hierarchical clustering, and diagnosis-stratified herb-use heatmaps. At least one prespecified history keyword was detected in 474 visits (85.41%). When permitted by institutional policy, a human-supervised artificial intelligence (AI) option may assist with terminology checks, cross-file consistency review, and caption-figure alignment. Any use of AI must be documented in a separate audit record and must not replace source-data review. By integrating governance, normalization, computation, clinical interpretation, and visual output into a single reproducible workflow, the method transforms dispersed clinical documentation into a reviewable research resource. The protocol can be adapted to other expert-practice datasets, multicenter terminology projects, and prospective clinical data platforms.

papers.title: Research Trends in Acupuncture for Cancer Pain: A Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.authors: Hu F, Xu W, Gu W, Yuan S, Guo Y, Lu J et al.
papers.abstract: Approximately 44% of cancer patients experience pain, with over 50% affected in advanced stages. Opioid therapy, though standard, carries significant side effects. Acupuncture, a traditional Chinese therapy, has shown potential in relieving cancer pain with minimal adverse reactions. This study used bibliometric methods to identify research hotspots and frontiers in acupuncture for cancer pain. Publications (2010-2025) were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed, and Scopus. CiteSpace 6.4.R1 and VOSviewer 1.6.20 were used for bibliometric and thematic analysis, examining countries, institutions, authors, journals, co-cited references, and keywords. The literature selection process was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A total of 2,139 publications were included, showing an overall increasing trend. China led in publication volume; Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) was the most productive institution; J. Mao was the most productive author; and J Clin Oncol was the most cited journal. Core keywords included "acupuncture", "breast cancer", "pain", "quality of life", "management", "cancer pain", and "electroacupuncture". Cluster analysis generated 15 thematic clusters. Emerging themes included acupoint stimulation, complementary therapies, symptom management, integrative medicine, and clinical evaluation. This study maps 16-year trends in acupuncture for cancer pain, revealing collaborations, hotspots, and emerging directions to guide future research.

papers.title: Identification of Heme Metabolism-Related Biomarkers in Keloids Using Transcriptomic Analysis and Cultured Human Fibroblasts.
papers.authors: Yang Q, Zhang J, Sun X, Wang J
papers.abstract: Keloid is a fibroproliferative disorder with high recurrence and unclear pathogenesis, lacking effective therapeutic targets. Recent evidence suggests metabolic reprogramming, particularly in heme metabolism, may drive fibrosis. This study investigates the role of heme metabolism, focusing on feline leukemia virus subgroup C receptor 1 (FLVCR1), in keloid pathogenesis and explores its diagnostic and therapeutic potential. We analyzed bulk RNA-seq datasets and single-cell RNA-seq data (scRNA-seq). Differential expression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and random forest (RF) models identified heme metabolism-related diagnostic biomarkers. Immune infiltration, single-cell mapping, microRNA (miRNA) network construction, and molecular docking with traditional Chinese medicine compounds were performed. Six heme metabolism-related biomarkers were identified, forming a diagnostic nomogram with high accuracy. FLVCR1, enriched in endothelial cells and melanocytes, correlated negatively with T follicular helper cells, suggesting immunometabolic crosstalk. MiRNA regulatory network analysis revealed five miRNAs co-targeting all six biomarkers. Molecular docking identified (+)-gallocatechin as a high-affinity FLVCR1 ligand. These findings suggest an association between FLVCR1-related heme metabolism and immune alterations in keloid pathogenesis. The biomarker panel showed exploratory diagnostic potential, and (+)-gallocatechin was identified as a candidate FLVCR1-interacting compound requiring further validation. This study reframes keloid within the metabo-fibrotic spectrum and proposes metabolic-immune intervention as a novel therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Berberine attenuates diabetic kidney injury via FOXO1/SP1-associated regulation of renal SGLT-2 expression.
papers.authors: Pan J, Wang X, Han X, Cheng H, Zhang F, Chen Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Berberine (BBR), a plant-derived isoquinoline alkaloid, has been reported to exert anti-hyperglycemic and renoprotective effects. However, the mechanism by which BBR regulates renal glucose transport under diabetic conditions remains unclear. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2), mainly expressed in renal proximal tubular epithelial cells, plays a key role in renal glucose reabsorption. This study investigated whether BBR attenuates diabetic kidney injury by regulating SGLT-2 expression and examined the potential involvement of FOXO1 and SP1 in this regulation.
Db/db mice and high-glucose-exposed human kidney-2 (HK-2) cells were used to evaluate the effects of BBR, empagliflozin (EM), and their combination. Metabolic and renal phenotypes were assessed by biochemical, histological, and ultrastructural analyses. Network pharmacology, public transcriptomic data mining, molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), quantitative real-time PCR, western blotting, immunofluorescence, nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation, co-immunoprecipitation, 2-NBDG uptake, dual-luciferase reporter assays, FOXO1 overexpression, and pharmacological interference with SP1-associated regulation were performed to investigate the regulatory mechanism.
Both BBR and EM improved metabolic abnormalities and renal injury in db/db mice, whereas combined treatment produced marked metabolic and renal improvements but was accompanied by an increasing trend in AST. BBR reduced hyperglycemia, improved glucose tolerance and enhanced the glucose-lowering response to exogenous insulin during the ITT, suppressed urinary albumin excretion, and alleviated renal histopathological and ultrastructural damage. Molecular docking and qualitative CETSA findings suggested that FOXO1 may represent a potential molecular target of BBR. In HK-2 cells, high-glucose stimulation increased SGLT-2 expression and glucose uptake, accompanied by dysregulation of FOXO1 and SP1 signaling. BBR downregulated FOXO1 and SGLT-2, restored SP1 and phosphorylated FOXO1 levels, and reduced glucose uptake under high-glucose conditions. FOXO1 overexpression attenuated the BBR-induced reduction in SGLT-2 expression, whereas pharmacological interference with SP1-associated regulation further supported the functional involvement of SP1 in SGLT-2 regulation.
BBR attenuates diabetic kidney injury, at least in part, through FOXO1/SP1-associated regulation of renal SGLT-2 expression. These findings support the involvement of a FOXO1/SP1-associated regulatory axis in renal tubular glucose handling under diabetic conditions.

papers.title: The Role of Traditional Chinese Medicine in the Treatment of Lupus Nephritis.
papers.authors: Liu R, Wen Q, Yu J, Yang X, Chen W
papers.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) represents one of the most severe organ manifestations of systemic lupus erythematosus and remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in affected patients. Its pathogenesis is highly complex, involving multifaceted immune dysregulation and posing substantial challenges for clinical management. According to Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), LN is characterized by root deficiency and branch excess, with kidney deficiency as the base and heat-toxins combined with blood stasis driving disease progression. Furthermore, clinical manifestations of LN vary significantly across disease stages and are often complicated by conventional pharmacotherapies. Accumulating clinical evidence increasingly supports the therapeutic efficacy of TCM intervention in LN management. Pharmacologic investigations have further elucidated their multi-target, pleiotropic actions, including modulating immune responses and regulating critical molecular pathways implicated in the pathogenesis of LN. This review systematically outlines the TCM conceptualization of LN pathogenesis; catalogs commonly employed compound formulas, single herbs, and bioactive extracts used in clinical practice; and delineates their underlying pharmacologic mechanisms, thereby providing a rigorous scientific foundation for rational TCM formulation design and facilitating the development of integrated, evidence-informed, and optimized therapeutic strategies for LN.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine for Helicobacter pylori Infection in the Antibiotic-Resistance Era: Ethnopharmacological Evidence, Mechanisms, and Host-Pathogen Modulation.
papers.authors: Zhang K, Zhao Y, Yang Y, Wang Y, Shang H, Pu J et al.
papers.abstract:
Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection remains a global health burden, and antibiotic resistance has reduced the effectiveness of standard eradication regimens. In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), persistent infection is interpreted as retention of pathogenic factors in the spleen-stomach system. Herbal formulas are investigated as adjunctive strategies, but their clinical roles and mechanistic basis require clarification.
To develop a host-pathogen modulation framework integrating clinical evidence, antibiotic resistance and persistence mechanisms, and TCM pharmacology, while distinguishing clinically supported effects from preclinical plausibility.
This critical narrative review was based on a structured search of six databases from inception through April 2026. Evidence was synthesized without quantitative pooling.
Some TCM formulas used with standard regimens were associated with improved eradication outcomes, whereas others showed similar eradication rates with possible advantages in symptom relief, tolerability, or adverse-event reduction. However, confidence in the clinical evidence remains low because most studies were small, single-center trials with heterogeneous interventions and comparators, incomplete risk-of-bias reporting, inconsistent outcome definitions, limited follow-up, and inadequate safety assessment. Preclinical studies suggest that formulas, herbs, and compounds may affect bacterial growth and colonization fitness, urease, adhesion, virulence systems, biofilm-associated tolerance, mucosal injury, inflammation, and gastric-gut microecology. Interpretation of these mechanisms is further limited by inconsistent quantitative pharmacological data, uncertain gastric exposure and pharmacokinetics, and weak linkage between experimental findings and clinical outcomes.
TCM should not replace standard eradication therapy. Its more defensible role is as a potential host-pathogen modulatory strategy with adjunctive, supportive, and mucosa-protective value. The current clinical findings should be regarded as preliminary rather than confirmatory. Rigorous multicenter trials, standardized interventions, quantitative pharmacology, pharmacokinetic validation, and mechanism-linked clinical studies are required.

papers.title: Association of governor vessel fire dragon moxibustion with patient-reported sleep quality and proteinuria in early stage diabetic kidney disease: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Mao L, Wen X, Zou Z
papers.abstract:
Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and comorbid insomnia form a pernicious bidirectional cycle that accelerates renal decline. Despite optimal guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), a substantial residual risk of proteinuria persists. This study aimed to examine the association of adjunctive Governor Vessel fire dragon moxibustion with patient-reported sleep quality, renal parameters, and documented safety outcomes in patients with early stage DKD, comorbid insomnia, and Spleen and Kidney Yang Deficiency.
In this retrospective cohort study, 286 eligible patients were initially enrolled to receive either standard GDMT alone or GDMT combined with a 4-week course of fire dragon moxibustion. To reduce measured baseline confounding, 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was conducted, generating 82 well-balanced patient pairs (N = 164). The primary outcome was the change in the patient-reported Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) global score. Exploratory secondary outcomes included 4-week changes in 24-h urinary protein (24 h-Upro), urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and fasting plasma glucose (FPG).
In the matched cohort, the moxibustion group achieved a significantly greater mean reduction in the global PSQI score than the standard care group (- 5.3 ± 1.8 vs. - 1.3 ± 1.1; P < 0.001), indicating a greater improvement in patient-reported sleep quality. Exploratory analyses showed greater 4-week reductions in 24 h-Upro (- 0.07 ± 0.06 vs. - 0.02 ± 0.05 g/24 h; P < 0.001) and UACR (- 23.9 ± 15.4 vs. - 5.8 ± 12.5 mg/g; P < 0.001). Changes in eGFR and FPG did not differ significantly between the two groups (both P > 0.05). Three patients (3.7%) experienced mild, transient localized skin reactions, and no severe adverse events were recorded.
Adjunctive Governor Vessel fire dragon moxibustion was associated with greater 4-week improvement in patient-reported sleep quality among patients with early stage DKD and insomnia and was generally well tolerated. Exploratory analyses also showed greater short-term reductions in 24-h urinary protein excretion and albuminuria, but their stabilization, durability, and long-term renal significance remain uncertain. Because treatment was not blinded and sleep quality was assessed using the self-reported PSQI, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in prospective studies incorporating an appropriate sham or attention-matched control, objective sleep measures, repeated urinary measurements, and longer renal follow-up.

papers.title: Rethinking Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder: A Systems-Level Disorder of Stress Dysregulation and the Role of Complementary and Alternative Medicine.
papers.authors: Yang EJ, Park HR
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is traditionally viewed as a brain-centered disorder characterized by impaired fear extinction and dysregulated emotional processing. Despite advances in pharmacologic and psychotherapeutic interventions, treatment resistance remains a major challenge for a substantial proportion of patients, highlighting the complexity of PTSD pathophysiology beyond central neural mechanisms. In addition, PTSD is associated with persistent dysregulation of systemic stress-regulatory networks, including the autonomic nervous system, immune-inflammatory pathways, and the gut-brain axis. This Opinion proposes that complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) interventions may exert therapeutic effects in PTSD by restoring disrupted homeostatic regulation across these interconnected systems. CAM modalities, such as acupuncture, herbal medicine, yoga, and breathing-based practices, may converge on common regulatory targets, including enhancement of vagal tone, modulation of inflammation, and stabilization of gut-brain communication. We propose that inconsistent clinical outcomes of CAM interventions in patients with PTSD may reflect, in part, inadequate patient stratification and outcome measures rather than an absence of therapeutic effects. Reconceptualizing PTSD as a disorder of systemic stress dysregulation provides a framework for investigating how CAM interventions might contribute mechanistically to an integrated, precision-oriented treatment paradigm.

papers.title: Sourness in the flesh: cultural shaping of somatic experience in Mandarin Chinese.
papers.authors: Huang S, Chen CC
papers.abstract: In some Sino-Tibetan languages, the gustatory term meaning 'sour' is widely used to describe somatosensory states such as muscle aches, exertional soreness, and tender sensations during acupuncture: a sensation called sngception. This study draws from the fields of linguistic anthropology, medical humanities, and corpus linguistics to investigate the cultural-historical and cognitive basis of sngception. Through a corpus analysis of modern Mandarin Chinese, the current study examined the semantic patterns and collocations of suān () 'sour.' With current medical findings on acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs), the sourness metaphor emerges as both physiologically and culturally grounded. Such cultural-linguistic frameworks play a significant role in shaping how discomfort is perceived and interpreted, which calls for greater attention to clinical awareness of culturally embedded expressions of pain in intercultural healthcare settings.

papers.title: Evaluating the accuracy of full text and serial screening by one versus two independent reviewers: Part 2 of a meta-research study of rapid review methodological trade-offs.
papers.authors: Corso M, Ead L, Brunton G, Negrini S, Tricco AC, Côté P
papers.abstract:
We aimed to determine the accuracy of one versus two reviewers for full-text screening, and serial screening (title/abstract and full text). We also determined the inter-rater reliability, post-test probability (PTP), false positive and negative rates, and sources of misclassification.
One reviewer screened fulltext articles from three systematic reviews evaluating interventions (acupuncture, education and TENS) for chronic low back pain. We combined these results with titles and abstracts screened by the same reviewer to assess serial screening accuracy (screening title and abstracts then full text studies). Outcomes were compared to consensus decisions from two independent reviewers. We computed sensitivity, specificity, positive (PPV) and negative predictive values (NPV) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Inter-rater reliability (Cohen's kappa) and positive PTP for serial screening were calculated. Rates and reasons for misclassification were examined. A sensitivity analysis of English studies explored the impact of AI-assisted translation of non-English studies.
A total of 120, 92 and 91 studies were screened for the acupuncture, education, and TENS reviews, respectively. Compared with two reviewers, the sensitivity of single reviewer full-text screening ranged from 62% to 88%, specificity from 84% to 96%, PPV from 70% to 77% and NPV from 89% to 97%. Kappa ranged from 0.61 to 0.73. Single reviewer sensitivity for serial screening ranged from 62% to 81%, specificity from 98% to 100%, PPV from 68% to 71% and NPV was 99%. Kappa ranged from 0.67 to 0.73. Positive PTP ranged from 42.7% to 63.5%. Misclassifications were mostly due to interpretation of the population, interventions or comparators. There were no or small differences in the estimates with overlap of CIs between English and all language analyses.
The accuracy of one versus two reviewers may be reduced in serial screening, resulting in missed and falsely included studies, ranging across reviews. Therefore, there is uncertainty around whether a single reviewer can correctly select relevant studies. However, the impact on rapid review results is unknown. Although overall agreement is substantial, reporting sensitivity and specificity can provide insight into classifications between reviewers. Carefully defining the population, intervention and comparators in screening is required and highlights the need for improved reporting in trials.

papers.title: Shenhuang Granules regulate the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway to alleviate pyroptosis of pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells.
papers.authors: Wan C, Lu J, Xu L, Jiang M, Zhu C, Zhang W et al.
papers.abstract:
Shenhuang Granules (SHG) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula composed of six medicinal materials: Panax ginseng C.A. Mey. (Ginseng Radix et Rhizoma), Rheum palmatum L. (Rhei Radix et Rhizoma), Sargentodoxa cuneata (Oliv.) Rehder & E.H. Wilson (Sargentodoxae Caulis), Taraxacum mongolicum Hand. -Mazz. (Taraxaci Herba), Aconitum carmichaelii Debeaux (Aconiti Lateralis Radix Praeparata), and Whitmania pigra Whitman (Hirudo). According to TCM theory, this formula is designed to replenish Qi and strengthen the body's resistance, clear heat and remove toxins, and promote blood circulation to eliminate blood stasis. In clinical practice, SHG has been used as an adjunctive therapy for sepsis, showing beneficial effects in ameliorating systemic inflammatory responses and microcirculatory disturbances. However, the underlying pharmacological mechanisms remain largely unclear.
To validate that SHG and its active monomers alleviate sepsis-induced lung injury through targeted suppression of the NLRP3-driven PMVEC pyroptosis pathway.
The chemical composition of SHG was analyzed by UHPLC-MS/MS. In vivo, SA-ARDS was induced in C57BL/6J mice by cecal ligation and puncture (CLP), with SHG (61.85 mg/mouse/d), its monomers, (-)-epicatechin gallate (ECG) and gallic acid (GA) (20 mg/kg/d), or the NLRP3 inhibitor MCC950 (10 mg/kg/d), were administered via intraperitoneal injection for 3 days prior to modeling. Lung injury severity and activation of the pyroptosis pathway were evaluated using histopathology, transmission electron microscopy, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and ELISA. In vitro, LPS-stimulated (1 μg/mL) PMVECs were used to screen 43 monomers, and the underlying mechanisms were subsequently verified.
Compared with the Model group, SHG treatment significantly attenuated body weight loss in mice (P < 0.001), reduced the lung wet-to-dry (W/D) weight ratio (P < 0.05), and decreased Evans blue extravasation in lung tissues (P < 0.01). SHG also significantly downregulated the mRNA expression levels of pyroptosis-related genes, including Twik2, Nlrp3, Asc, Caspase-1, and Gsdmd, in lung tissues (all P < 0.01), and markedly reduced the protein expression of NLRP3, ASC, pro-Caspase-1, and Caspase-1 (all P < 0.05). ELISA results further demonstrated that SHG significantly decreased serum levels of the inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-γ, IL-18, pro-IL-1β, and pro-IL-18 in mice (all P < 0.05). In vitro, compared with the Model group, SHG significantly suppressed the transcriptional levels of Twik2, Nlrp3, Asc, Caspase-1, and Gsdmd in PMVECs (all P < 0.05), and reduced the protein expression of NLRP3, ASC, GSDMD, GSDMD-NT, and IL-1β (all P < 0.05). Additionally, SHG markedly decreased lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release (P < 0.0001) and attenuated extracellular potassium ion (K+) efflux (P < 0.0001). Notably, ECG and GA individually exhibited potent inhibitory effects on PMVEC pyroptosis. Compared with the Model group, both ECG and GA significantly suppressed mRNA expression of Twik2, Nlrp3, Asc, Caspase-1, and Gsdmd (all P < 0.05) and reduced protein levels of NLRP3, ASC, Caspase-1, and GSDMD (all P < 0.05). Moreover, ECG significantly inhibited GSDMD-NT and IL-1β protein expression (all P < 0.05). Both ECG and GA markedly reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and pro-IL-18 levels (all P < 0.05), and GA additionally suppressed IL-18 and pro-IL-1β expression (all P < 0.01). Furthermore, both ECG and GA significantly decreased LDH release (P < 0.0001) and inhibited extracellular K+ efflux (P < 0.0001). However, this study has several limitations, including a small sample size, the absence of dose-gradient and time-course analyses, insufficient functional validation of the TWIK2 channel, and the lack of quantitative pharmacokinetic and synergy analyses, which should be addressed in future studies.
Shenhuang Granules attenuated PMVEC pyroptosis and ameliorated sepsis-induced lung injury by suppressing TWIK2 and the downstream NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway, with GA and ECG as the key active components.

papers.title: Shenghui decoction improves sleep-deprivation-induced cognitive impairment in mice by modulating neuroinflammation, NRG1/ErbB4 signaling, and purine metabolism.
papers.authors: Lei Y, Tan J, Zhang M, Zhang S, Xia J, Yin C et al.
papers.abstract:
Shenghui Decoction (SHD) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula first documented by Chen Shiduo in Bian Zheng Lu during the Qing dynasty. It has traditionally been used for disorders related to forgetfulness, insomnia, and mental disturbance. Cognitive impairment induced by sleep deprivation (SD) shares features with these traditional indications. However, the mechanisms underlying the protective effects of SHD against SD-induced cognitive impairment remain unclear.
This study aimed to evaluate the protective effects of SHD against SD-induced cognitive impairment in mice and investigate potential mechanisms involving neuroinflammation, NRG1/ErbB4-related synaptic plasticity, and metabolic homeostasis.
Male C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned to five groups: the negative control group (Control), SD model group (Model), melatonin group (MT, 100 mg/kg), low-dose SHD group (SHD-L, 13.5 g/kg), and high-dose SHD group (SHD-H, 27 g/kg). Mice received intragastric treatment once daily for 21 consecutive days, and 72-h SD was initiated on day 18 using a modified multiple-platform water-environment method. Cognitive function was evaluated using the novel object recognition test and Morris water maze. Hippocampal histopathology was assessed by hematoxylin and eosin and Nissl staining. Western blotting was used to quantify hippocampal levels of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), NRG1, ErbB4, phosphorylated ErbB4 (p-ErbB4), parvalbumin (PV), postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD95), and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). Network pharmacology analysis was performed using the 15 blood-absorbed prototype constituents of SHD identified in our previous study. Untargeted serum metabolomics was subsequently conducted using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry. Finally, network pharmacology and metabolomics data were integrated for joint analysis.
SD significantly impaired recognition and spatial learning and memory. These behavioral deficits were accompanied by marked histopathological changes in the hippocampal dentate gyrus and cornu ammonis 3 regions. SHD-H significantly ameliorated both the behavioral and histopathological abnormalities. SD also increased hippocampal IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α levels, while reducing NRG1, PV, PSD95, and BDNF levels and the p-ErbB4/ErbB4 ratio. SHD-H reversed these changes to varying degrees. Network pharmacology identified 88 core targets. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analysis highlighted Ras signaling pathways, PI3K-Akt signaling pathways, MAPK signaling pathways, and ErbB signaling pathways. Untargeted serum metabolomics identified 48 differential metabolites altered by SD. Pathway enrichment analysis showed that these metabolites were mainly associated with glycerophospholipid metabolism, sphingolipid metabolism, and purine metabolism. SHD-H shifted these metabolic alterations toward the Control profile to varying degrees. A MetScape-based metabolite-reaction-enzyme-gene network was constructed to identify genes associated with the 48 differential metabolites. Intersecting these metabolite-associated genes with the 88 core network pharmacology targets yielded four candidate overlapping targets: APRT, NT5M, ADK, and HPRT1. Further analysis of the metabolite-reaction-enzyme-gene network linked all four candidate targets to deoxyguanosine-related metabolic reactions. The four candidate targets were then mapped back to the predicted target profiles of the 15 blood-absorbed prototype constituents of SHD. This analysis identified morroniside, loganin, and ginsenoside Rb1 as blood-absorbed prototype constituents predicted to be associated with one or more of these candidate targets. Molecular docking further suggested favorable potential interactions between these constituents and their corresponding candidate targets.
SHD ameliorated SD-induced cognitive impairment and hippocampal histopathological damage in mice. These effects were associated with reduced hippocampal neuroinflammation and partial normalization of NRG1/ErbB4-related PV and synaptic plasticity markers. Integrated network pharmacology and metabolomics analyses further suggest that purine metabolism may represent a potential link between SD-induced systemic metabolic disturbances and the effects of SHD. These findings provide experimental evidence for the pharmacological basis of the traditional use of SHD for conditions associated with forgetfulness, insomnia, and mental disturbance.

papers.title: ROS responsive micelles coloaded with Linezolid and Honokiol for targeting and synergistic therapy of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus pneumonia.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Bi Y, Wang X, Xu J, Dai M, Wang S et al.
papers.abstract: The growing crisis of bacterial resistance has prompted the development of novel antibacterial therapeutic systems to combat Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) pneumonia. This study reports a nano-micelle system (RMLH-Ms) for the co-delivery of the antibiotic Linezolid and the traditional Chinese medicine monomer Honokiol. Antibacterial peptide Magainin II (Mag II) was employed to endow the micelles with bacterial targeting ability, and thioketal bond modification was used to confer ROS-responsive properties. Linezolid and Honokiol were successfully encapsulated into micelles with entrapment efficiencies (EE%>95%.) A low critical micelle concentration (CMC) of 0.0138 mg/mL and sustained colloidal stability over 21 days were observed. Mag II‑modified RMLH‑Ms appeared to show improved bacterial targeting ability compared with unmodified micelles. The ZIP score for Linezolid and Honokiol combination was 7.61, exhibiting a synergistic antibacterial effect. Micelles incorporated with honokiol (LH-Ms) reduced the MIC of L-Ms from 4 μg/mL to 2 μg/mL. Furthermore, the incorporation of Honokiol also exhibited additional anti-inflammatory, macrophage polarization regulation immune microenvironment regulating activities in vitro. In vivo, The survival rates were 12.5%, 37.5%, 50%, 62.5%, and 75% for the model group, L-Ms, LH-Ms, MLH-Ms, and RMLH-Ms group, respectively. The survival rate of the RMLH-Ms group rose by 62.5% compared with the model group. RMLH-Ms induced mild decreases in lung bacterial burden, mitigated inflammatory responses and alleviated pathological lung damage, exhibiting favorable in vivo activity under experimental conditions.

summary.clinical_takeaway: 호노키올은 항균제와의 병용에서 보조적 항균·항염 효과를 보일 가능성이 있으나, 이는 전임상 결과이므로 임상 적용 근거로는 부족하다.

papers.title: Alleviation of hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury by ginsenoside Rg5 and deoxyandrographolide through inhibition of SLC7A11/GPX4-mediated ferroptosis.
papers.authors: Su W, Li Y, Liu B, Dong R, Zeng Q, Tu J et al.
papers.abstract: Shenfu Injection is a traditional Chinese medicine formulation widely used for cardiovascular and ischemic disorders. This study investigated the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of its bioactive constituents, ginsenoside Rg5 (Rg5) and deoxyandrographolide (DA), against hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI). Mouse HIRI models and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-treated AML12 cells were used for in vivo and in vitro studies, respectively. Combined Rg5 and DA treatment alleviated hepatic histopathological injury, reduced serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels, restored antioxidant capacity, and decreased inflammatory responses and hepatocyte apoptosis. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses indicated that ferroptosis, glutathione metabolism, and lipid peroxidation-related pathways were involved in the protective effects of Rg5 and DA. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted interactions between Rg5 or DA and the ferroptosis-related proteins SLC7A11 and GPX4. Moreover, combined treatment increased SLC7A11 and GPX4 expression at both the mRNA and protein levels and decreased PTGS2 mRNA expression in vivo and in vitro. These findings suggest that Rg5 and DA protect against HIRI, by regulating SLC7A11/GPX4-associated ferroptosis, while also attenuating inflammation and hepatocyte apoptosis.

summary.clinical_takeaway: 본 연구는 Shenfu Injection의 구성 성분이 허혈성 간손상에서 산화스트레스와 페롭토시스 억제와 연관될 수 있음을 시사하지만, 전임상 결과이므로 임상적 적용은 추가 검증이 필요하다.

papers.title: Synergistic Polyphenol Recovery From Embelia ribes Using MP-UAE, UAE, and MAE and In Silico Studies Against HCV Protease.
papers.journal: Journal of analytical methods in chemistry
papers.authors: Imtiaz F, Ahmed D, Zumar S, Al-Mijalli SH, Iqbal M
papers.abstract: Embelia ribes (ER) is well regarded in herbal medicine for its therapeutic properties, making the development of efficient methods to obtain its bioactive extracts of high yield essential. This study evaluated and optimized three extraction techniques, microwave-pretreated ultrasound-assisted extraction (MP-UAE), ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE), and microwave-assisted extraction (MAE), to isolate bioactive compounds from ER seeds. Embelin, a primary bioactive, was quantified in the optimized extracts, while 13 bioactives, including embelin, were analyzed through in silico studies targeting HCV NS3 protease. Process optimization using response surface methodology (RSM) focused on key parameters: total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), DPPH radical scavenging activity (DRSA), and ABTS radical scavenging activity (ARSA). Experimental results validated the models, with MP-UAE yielding the highest TPC (183.00 mg GAE/g DW), TFC (54.54 mg RE/g DW), DRSA (72.80%), and ARSA (81.33%). Optimized conditions included microwave power of 238 W, 48-min sonication, and a 19-mL/g solvent-to-plant ratio for MP-UAE. Embelin content, measured spectrophotometrically, was highest in MP-UAE at 39.98 ± 0.97 mg/g DW. Molecular docking using Maestro 12.5 identified amentoflavone (-8.991 kcal/mol), embelin (-8.152 kcal/mol), quercetin (-8.107 kcal/mol), and aloe-emodin (-8.014 kcal/mol) as top compounds, surpassing the standard drug boceprevir (-5.342 kcal/mol). This study establishes a green, efficient extraction method for ER seed bioactives, highlighting the antiviral potential of embelin and contributing to herb-based pharmaceutical advancements, particularly in antiviral drug development.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine for Alzheimer's disease: pathological mechanisms and multi-target interventions.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Song R, Wang J, Chen B, Sun H, Ren X et al.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder driven by multiple interconnected pathological mechanisms. This narrative review systematically searched major biomedical databases for relevant literature published between 2015 and 2026, using predefined keywords combined with manual supplementary searches. Two independent reviewers performed a qualitative screening based on relevance, involving the iterative review of titles, abstracts, and full texts. A targeted selection of representative, high-quality studies centered on TCM and AD pathogenesis/mechanisms was then conducted. Ultimately, studies were included in the narrative review for the mechanistic synthesis of TCM against AD. This review summarizes seven core AD mechanisms, including the Aβ cascade, Tau abnormalities, Neuroinflammation, Regulated cell death, Synaptic plasticity impairment, Gut microbiota-brain axis imbalance, and Oxidative stress, and critically discusses the multi‑target interventions of TCM via key molecules such as GSK-3β, BACE1, SIRT1, NF‑κB, NLRP3, PINK1/Parkin, AMPK, BDNF, PSD‑95, and the Nrf2/HO‑1 pathway. GSK‑3β and NF‑κB act as central hubs linking Aβ/Tau pathology to neuroinflammation, while AMPK, SIRT1, and Nrf2/HO‑1 regulate metabolic and redox homeostasis, PINK1/Parkin control mitophagy, and BDNF/PSD‑95 determine synaptic integrity. TCM's therapeutic superiority lies in its simultaneous modulation of this entire hierarchical network, representing a multi‑target strategy that conventional single‑target drugs cannot replicate. By concurrently modulating these distinct yet interacting nodes, TCM establishes a synergistic therapeutic network that reduces Aβ deposition, attenuates Tau hyperphosphorylation, and mitigates neuronal damage, offering a novel direction for future AD research.

papers.title: Longxue tongluo capsule enhances ischemic stroke recovery via microbiota-metabolite-gene interactions.
papers.authors: Ren G, Yang W, Wang J, Zhang J, Gao H, Gao X et al.
papers.abstract: The gut-brain axis represents an emerging therapeutic target. This study seeks to investigate the regulatory effects of LXTL on the brain-gut axis and to elucidate its mechanism of action during the ischemic stroke recovery period. This study investigated the effects of LXTL on a middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion model. The assessment of recovery effects was conducted through the evaluation of brain injury scores, Y-maze performance, open field tests. Furthermore, comprehensive analyses were conducted on the gut microbiota, damaged brain tissue, cecal contents, and brain samples using metagenomic sequencing, transcriptomic sequencing, and non-targeted metabolomics. And the selected targets were verified. Integrated analyses were conducted by constructing correlation networks and performing joint pathway enrichment to elucidate the connections between microbial alterations, metabolite changes, and gene expression modifications. LXTL improved cognitive and exploratory behaviors, reduced brain damage and neuron loss, and enhanced gut health by increasing beneficial bacteria like Eubacterium and Kurthia. It boosted SCFAs, neuroactive metabolites, and altered nucleotide metabolism. LXTL is linked to genes involved in neurorepair and immune homeostasis, correlates with microglial polarization, and is associated with genes such as Ngfr, Card9, Chat, Nkg7, and Gch1 within the pertinent pathways. The integrated network linked LXTL-enhanced microbiota, gut and brain metabolites, and repair genes, facilitating recovery through a neurorepair-immune-metabolic triad. LXTL aids ischemic stroke recovery by altering gut microbiota and gut-brain metabolite profiles, while regulating brain gene networks related to neuroplasticity, inflammation, and metabolism. This demonstrates LXTL's multi-target effects through the gut-brain axis, underscoring the potential of herbal medicine in stroke rehabilitation.

papers.title: 3D-Printed hydroxysafflor yellow A/hydrogel porous scaffolds for bone regeneration.
papers.authors: Mo T, Hong Y, Gao Y, Yang Y, Chen H, Niu G et al.
papers.abstract: The integration of angiogenesis with osteogenesis is crucial for the success of scaffolds in treating bone defects. Here, we present a strategy to address this challenge by engineering a 3D-printed porous scaffold that delivers hydroxysafflor yellow A (HSYA), a pro-angiogenic and osteogenic compound from traditional Chinese medicine, within a GelMA/HAMA hydrogel matrix. An optimized 8% GelMA/2% HAMA bioink provided excellent printability, fidelity, and porosity, enabling the fabrication of scaffolds with sustained HSYA release over four weeks. In vitro, the scaffold demonstrated excellent biocompatibility and concurrently enhanced the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs and the angiogenic activity of HUVECs. In a rat cranial defect model, this dual bioactivity resulted in a bone volume fraction close to 35% at 8 weeks, accompanied by significantly improved local blood perfusion. By synergistically merging a traditional Chinese medicine-derived active molecule with advanced 3D printing technology, this study offers a promising strategy for vascularized bone regeneration.

papers.title: Acupuncture is associated with reduced cholecystectomy rate and preservation of hepatobiliary and renal function in biliary disorders: A propensity score-matched real-world cohort study.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Chen CY, Hung CK, Shi HY, Luo Y, Huang CY, Hung KS
papers.abstract:
To investigate the association between acupuncture and 5-year cholecystectomy rate, alongside hepatorenal function preservation, in a large-scale real-world cohort of patients with biliary disorders.
A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 7930 patients who had received manual acupuncture were compared with 7930 matched controls. The primary outcome was 5-year cumulative cholecystectomy rate, assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and risk ratio.
After matching, all baseline covariates achieved a standardized mean difference below 0.1. The acupuncture group demonstrated significantly lower 5-year cumulative cholecystectomy rate (7.585% vs 13.454%; risk ratio: 0.564, 95% confidence interval: 0.511-0.622; hazard ratio: 0.525, 95% confidence interval: 0.473-0.582; p < 0.0001). Acupuncture was also associated with significantly lower risk across all seven secondary outcomes, including markers of systemic inflammation, cholestasis, and hepatorenal impairment (all p < 0.0001).
In this large-scale propensity score-matched cohort, manual acupuncture was significantly associated with reduced 5-year cholecystectomy rate and preservation of hepatobiliary and renal function in patients with biliary disorders.

papers.title: Cytochrome P450 enzymes in the biosynthesis of bioactive diterpenoids from traditional chinese medicinal plants.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Li W, Li H
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 enzymes play key catalytic roles in the biosynthesis of diterpenoid natural products from traditional Chinese medicinal plants. Operating through a conserved heme-thiolate catalytic cycle and Compound I-driven oxidation, these enzymes mediate most post-cyclization oxidative tailoring of diterpene scaffolds, including hydroxylation, epoxidation, carbon-skeleton rearrangement, and lactone formation. This review surveys the biosynthetic pathways of seven representative diterpenoids, namely tanshinones, paclitaxel, triptolide, andrographolide, ginkgolides, forskolin, and oridonin, in which sequential site-selective hydroxylation and multifunctional catalysis are recurring features, whereas carbon-skeleton remodeling proceeds through pathway-specific modes, including Wagner-Meerwein methyl migration in triptolide, NIH-shift alkyl migration and dual C-C bond cleavage in ginkgolides, and oxidative oxetane-ring formation in paclitaxel, with lactone ring construction observed in the andrographolide, triptolide, and ginkgolide pathways. Atomic-level studies of representative enzymes CYP76AH1, CYP725A4, TOT1, and TmCYP1 further clarify how substrate recognition, regioselectivity, and catalytic trajectories are governed within the active site, providing a basis for rational enzyme engineering. Finally, the prospects of artificial intelligence-assisted protein design for engineering P450 catalytic elements are discussed, encompassing structure prediction, protein language model-based mutational prescreening, and de novo catalytic-pocket design, along with their potential to facilitate heterologous biosynthesis and the sustainable production of bioactive diterpenoids from medicinal plants.

papers.title: [A randomized controlled study on application of giant needle electroacupuncture at different times for improving pain and joint function after total knee arthroplasty].
papers.journal: Zhongguo gu shang = China journal of orthopaedics and traumatology
papers.authors: Xu M, Shen J, Sun P, Wang J, Zhao C, Kang B et al.
papers.abstract:
To explore clinical efficacy of applying giant needle electroacupuncture at different times in improving pain and joint function after total knee arthroplasty(TKA).
A total of 120 patients who underwent TKA from July 2022 to March 2023 were included. They were divided into preoperative electro-acupuncture group, postoperative electro-acupuncture group, and control group according to different intervention times of electro-acupuncture, and 38 patients in each group, 2 patients from each group were dropped out, resulting in a final inclusion of 114 patients. In preoperative electro-acupuncture group, there were 7 males and 31 females;aged from 60 to 80 years old with an average of (72.0±5.8) years old;electro-acupuncture was performed on Weishu acupoint (ST32), Zusanli acupoint (ST36), Yinlingquan acupoint (SP9), and Yanglingquan acupoint (GB34) of non-operated lower limbs at 1 day before operation, 30 min before anesthesia induction, and 1 to 3 days after operation. In postoperative electro-acupuncture group, there were 9 males and 29 females;aged from 60 to 80 years old with average of (71.6±6.7) years old;the same acupuncture points and parameters were treated 1 to 3 days after operation. In control group, there were 6 males and 32 females;aged from 60 to 80 years old with an average of (71.6±7.1) years old;and were received pseudo-electroacupuncture treatment. Pain was scored at rest and during movement respectively before operation and 4 to 7 days after operation by using numerical rating scale at rest (NRSR) and numerical rating scale with movement (NRSM), joint function was evaluated by active range of motion (AROM) of knee joint, Hospital for Special Surgery(HSS) knee score, and Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC).
A total of 114 patients were followed up, with the follow-up period being 7 days after operation. There were no statistically significant differences in preoperative NRSR, NRSM, AROM, HSS, and WOMAC scores among three groups (P>0.05). There were statistically significant differences among three groups of NRSR and NRSM scores on the 4th to 7th day after operation (P<0.05). The comparison of AROM among three groups on the 7th day after operation showed statistically significant difference (P<0.05), while there was no statistically significant difference when comparing the data from 4 to 6 days after operation (P>0.05). The comparisons of HSS and WOMAC scores on the 7th day after operation among three groups showed statistically significant differences (P<0.05). NRSR scores of pre-electroacupuncture group on the 4th to 6th days after operation were 2.0(1.0, 2.3), 1.0(1.0, 2.0), and 1.0(1.0, 2.0) respectively, which were lower than those of post-electroacupuncture group 3.0(2.0, 4.0), 2.0(1.0, 3.0), 2.0(1.0, 2.0), and the differences were statistically significant (P<0.05). NRSM of preoperative electroacupuncture group on the 4th to 5th day after operation were 3.0(2.0, 3.0) and 2.0(1.0, 2.0), which were lower than those of postoperative electroacupuncture group 4.0(3.0, 5.0) and 3.0(2.0, 3.0), and the differences were statistically significant (P<0.05). HSS score of pre-electroacupuncture group on the 7th day after operation was (76.22±3.51), which was higher than that of post-electroacupuncture group (71.54±6.36), and the difference was statistically significant (P<0.05). WOMAC score of pre-electroacupuncture group on the 7th day after operation was(19.84±3.61), which was lower than that of post-electroacupuncture group (22.37±3.81), and the difference was statistically significant (P<0.05).
The application giant needle electroacupuncture before operation could better alleviate acute pain after TKA and improve function of knee joint.

papers.title: Anesthesia-Informed Approaches to Insomnia: Shared Neural Circuits, Biomimetic Sleep, and Emerging Interventional Strategies.
papers.authors: Wu Y, Yu X, Sun H, Huang F, Wang J
papers.abstract:
Insomnia affects approximately 10-30% of adults, burdening quality of life, cognition, and health. Although cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) and approved pharmacotherapies remain standard care, limited accessibility, durability, and efficacy in refractory populations have motivated interest in mechanism-based alternatives, including approaches derived from anesthetic pharmacology.
This narrative review examines the convergent neural circuits underlying anesthesia-induced and physiological sleep, critically appraises evidence for anesthetic agents-dexmedetomidine, ketamine/esketamine, and propofol-delivered through non-traditional modalities, and evaluates perioperative sleep optimization, with explicit attention to evidence level and limitations.
We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for English-language publications through June 2026. Evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs), systematic reviews, observational studies, case reports, and mechanistic studies was synthesized narratively and graded using the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine 2011 Levels of Evidence.
Dexmedetomidine induces "biomimetic sleep" via alpha-2 adrenergic agonism, resembling natural non-rapid eye movement stage 2 sleep more closely than propofol. However, most supporting evidence is mechanistic, perioperative, or from small pilot studies rather than insomnia-specific RCTs. Patient-controlled sleep systems, intranasal delivery, and bionic sleep therapy are promising but preliminary, with incomplete long-term safety data, particularly regarding cardiovascular effects and withdrawal. Ketamine and esketamine may enhance slow-wave sleep, but most data derive from comorbid depression, confounding attribution. Stellate ganglion block, acupuncture, and closed-loop stimulation remain investigational and susceptible to placebo effects. Perioperative strategies improve postoperative sleep in RCTs, but extrapolation to chronic insomnia is limited by fundamental etiological differences.
Anesthesia-informed approaches provide mechanistic insights and investigational directions rather than established alternatives to CBT-I or approved hypnotics. Priorities include adequately powered insomnia-specific RCTs, comparison with standard treatments, long-term safety evaluation, and phenotype-guided selection.

papers.title: Effects of Warm-Needling Acupuncture Plus Tuina on Inflammatory and Cartilage Biomarkers in Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Dong Y, Zeng K, Liu Y, Liang D, Xie G
papers.abstract:
Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) involves cartilage degeneration and synovial inflammation. Warm-needling acupuncture (WNA) plus Tuina is used clinically, but its systemic and local anti-inflammatory effects, as well as its potential benefits in modulating cartilage metabolism, lack robust evidence.
To systematically evaluate WNA plus Tuina's effects on inflammatory cytokines and cartilage biomarkers in KOA.
We searched 8 databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, SinoMed) to March 2026 for RCTs comparing WNA plus Tuina against single or conventional therapies. Outcomes included IL-1/IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, CRP, IL-17, and MMP-3. We used the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool and GRADE system.
A total of 19 RCTs were included. Meta-analysis revealed that compared with the control group, WNA combined with Tuina was associated with reduced systemic inflammation levels, including serum CRP (standardized mean difference [SMD] -2.58, 95% confidence interval [CI] [-4.49, -0.67]), IL-1/IL-1β (SMD -1.73, 95% CI [-3.00, -0.47]), IL-6 (SMD -2.19, 95% CI [-3.38, -0.99]), TNF-α (SMD -1.63, 95% CI [-2.92, -0.34]), and IL-17 (SMD -2.06, 95% CI [-3.49, -0.62]). Within the local joint microenvironment, the combined therapy also showed a greater decrease in synovial fluid IL-1/IL-1β (SMD -0.93) and TNF-α (SMD -1.60). Furthermore, the serum level of MMP-3, a cartilage degradation marker, appeared to be downregulated (SMD -2.77, 95% CI [-3.22, -2.31]). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these results. GRADE assessment indicated that the certainty of the evidence ranged from very low to low.
WNA combined with Tuina shows potential in reducing local and systemic inflammatory markers in KOA patients and may offer potential benefits in modulating cartilage metabolism. However, limited by the low certainty of current evidence, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and future validation through high-quality, large-scale RCTs is still required.

papers.title: Global characterization strategy for chemical constituent of traditional Chinese medicine formulas based on online comprehensive 2DLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS combined with deep learning clustering driven dual-mode acquisition: A case study of Qishen Yiqi Dropping Pills.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Yang M, Qin H, Wen J, Liu P, Wang X et al.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive characterization of the complex chemical constituents in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas remains a major challenge in elucidating their pharmacodynamic material basis and mechanisms of action. Although liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) is widely used for constituent identification, conventional acquisition strategies often fail to obtain sufficient fragment-ion information for both high- and low-abundance compounds co-eluting within the same retention-time window. To address this limitation, an online comprehensive two-dimensional liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry (2DLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS) platform was integrated with a dual-mode acquisition strategy driven by deep learning-based clustering. Deep learning-assisted mass defect filtering (MDF) was employed to classify precursor ions into specific chemical categories. The Python-based PyMassTime-Cluster system was then used to redistribute highly overlapping, co-eluting predicted ions into balanced sub-priority ion capture (sub-PIC) lists. These sub-PIC lists guided stepwise data-dependent acquisition (DDA), while data-independent acquisition (DIA) was incorporated as a complementary mode to improve overall fragment-ion coverage. This integrated workflow enabled efficient acquisition of MS/MS data for both high- and low-abundance constituents. Using this strategy, 181 compounds were characterized in Qishen Yiqi Dropping Pills (QSYQDP), including 49 flavonoids and their glycosides, 40 organic acids, 27 terpenoids, 12 phenylpropanoids, 10 saponins, 9 amino acids, and 34 other compounds. Overall, the integration of deep learning-based classification, retention-time clustering, and complementary acquisition modes provides an effective and transferable approach for the comprehensive chemical characterization of complex TCM formulas.

papers.title: Hederagenin Attenuates Morphine Addiction via GABAA1-Mediated Modulation of Ca2 +-CaMK-CREB Signaling in Ventral Tegmental Dopaminergic Neurons.
papers.authors: Jiang H, Zhou Z, Xue N, Deng J, Zhou Y, Lv X et al.
papers.abstract: Morphine-associated contextual reward learning promotes maladaptive drug-context associations during opioid exposure. Hederagenin (HE), a bioactive compound from traditional Chinese medicine, has neuroprotective potential, but its role in contextual reward learning remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of HE on morphine-induced conditioned place preference (CPP) acquisition and explored its target, downstream signaling, and brain-delivery strategy. HE attenuated morphine CPP acquisition in both sexes and reduced established CPP expression. Chemical proteomics identified the GABAA receptor α1 subunit (GABAA1, encoded by GABRA1) as a prioritized HE-associated target, supported by competitive pull-down, non-permeabilized HE-biotin labeling, microscale thermophoresis, cellular thermal shift assay, and molecular docking. Mechanistically, HE reduced c-Fos activation in ventral tegmental area (VTA) TH-positive dopaminergic neurons, attenuated reward-context-associated VTA calcium responses, suppressed intracellular Ca2 + elevation in SH-SY5Y cells, and reduced VTA CaMKII, PKA, and CREB phosphorylation. Animal-level analyses linked CPP scores to compartment-selective VTA calcium responses and p-CREB/CREB ratios, whereas TH+/c-Fos+ associations varied by treatment. Compared with non-targeted liposomes, RVG29-modified HE-loaded liposomes showed greater brain- and VTA-associated distribution and suppressed established CPP after a single administration. Together, these findings identify HE as a candidate modulator of morphine CPP through a GABAA1-related VTA Ca2 +-CaMK-cAMP-CREB mechanism and support RVG29 liposomes as an exploratory delivery strategy.

papers.title: A BSCB-Penetrating Nanoplatform for Enhanced Luteolin Delivery in PRMT2-Targeted Epigenetic Therapy of Spinal Cord Injury.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Jin B, Li S, Ouyang Q, Xiao Y, Wen J et al.
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a devastating disorder of the central nervous system (CNS) leading to irreversible neurological deficits. Effective pharmacotherapy remains elusive, due to the restrictive blood-spinal cord barrier (BSCB), underscoring the urgent need for targeted and efficient drug delivery strategies. Luteolin (LUT), a natural flavonoid with potent anti-neuroinflammatory properties, presents a promising therapeutic option; however, it is compromised by poor solubility, low bioavailability, and limited BSCB penetration. Drawing inspiration from the traditional Chinese medicine concept of the "orifice-opening" effect of borneol (BO), we developed BO-modified mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSN-BO@LUT) for targeted LUT delivery to the spinal cord. MSN-BO@LUT significantly enhanced LUT delivery to the spinal cord, achieving a 286.36-fold increase over LUT, and maintained a concentration of 802.17 ng/mL at 24 h. MSN-BO@LUT demonstrated robust anti-neuroinflammatory and neuroprotective effects in SCI mice, reducing microglial infiltration, promoting functional recovery, and showing favorable efficacy and safety compared with the positive control methylprednisolone. Mechanistically, released LUT targets protein arginine N-methyltransferase, reduces toll-like receptor 4 methylation, and inhibits nuclear factor kappa B-mediated pro-inflammatory signaling, thereby suppressing microglial M1 polarization. These findings suggest that MSN-BO@LUT not only provides a developed, safe, effective nanotherapeutic strategy for SCI treatment but also serves as a translatable template for developing precision nanomedicines targeting CNS disorders.

papers.title: Hepatoprotective Potential of Radix Astragali, a Qi-tonifying Traditional Herb: Modulation of Hepatocyte Energy Metabolism and Oxidative Homeostasis.
papers.authors: Sun X, Li X, Li S, Yang H, Zhang B
papers.abstract:
Radix Astragali (RA) is a widely utilized medicinal herb in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), known for its distinctive Qi-tonifying properties, with significant therapeutic efficacy in the treatment of diverse liver ailments. The pharmacological basis of TCM's Qi-tonifying effect primarily involves enhancing cellular vitality through the stimulation of energy metabolism and mitigation of oxidative stress, thereby facilitating the restoration of tissue and organ function.
This article presents a comprehensive review of the hepatoprotective effects of RA and its active constituents, focusing on their modulation of hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism, as well as oxidative homeostasis.
A thorough literature search was conducted using various online platforms and databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Scopus, up to July 2026. Keyword searches encompassed terms such as Radix Astragali, Huangqi Decoction, Astragalus polysaccharides, astragalosides, astragaloside IV, cycloastragenol, metabolic reprogramming, glucose metabolism, lipid metabolism, lipid deposition, blood glucose, oxidative stress, reactive oxygen species, liver diseases, and liver regeneration.
Recent advances in pharmacological research, particularly over the past decade-with a notable concentration of findings in the last three years-have further elucidated the hepatoprotective effects of Radix Astragali and its bioactive constituents in promoting hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism and maintaining oxidative homeostasis. Given the pivotal role of the hepatocellular aquaglyceroporin/peroxiporin aquaporin-9 (AQP9) in regulating hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism and oxidative homeostasis, and the ability of Radix Astragali and its active components to enhance AQP9 expression in hepatocytes and thereby promote liver regeneration, targeting AQP9-mediated glycerol and H2O2 transport may represent a potential therapeutic avenue for liver injury; however, the available evidence remains largely preclinical.
The augmentation of hepatocyte AQP9 expression underscores a significant scientific facet of RA's Qi-tonifying effect. AQP9 may represent a potential therapeutic target for liver injury, but its clinical relevance remains to be established. Future investigations should focus on identifying the specific active compounds and associated mechanisms responsible for upregulating AQP9 expression in RA.

papers.title: Quercetin-loaded exosomes prevent endometrial fibrosis by downregulating EGFR.
papers.authors: Zhang X, Zhu Y, Zhang X, Zhuang Q, Wang X, Zhang X et al.
papers.abstract: Intrauterine adhesions (IUA) are a common gynecological disorder characterized by endometrial fibrosis, driven by inflammation and stromal cell-to-myofibroblast transdifferentiation. IUA present significant clinical challenges due to high recurrence rates and drug resistance. While surgical adhesiolysis combined with estrogen therapy is the first-line treatment, its efficacy is limited in severe cases and relapse is common. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) offers a promising alternative, though the specific active components and mechanisms remain undefined. Here, we identified quercetin as a potent anti-fibrotic agent using network pharmacology; however, its clinical application is hindered by poor water solubility and low bioavailability. To overcome these limitations, we developed a quercetin-loaded exosome delivery system (Que-Exo). Compared to free quercetin, Que-Exo exhibited significantly superior anti-fibrotic efficacy at equivalent concentrations. Mechanistic investigations revealed that this therapeutic effect is mediated by the downregulation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), thereby inhibiting fibrosis progression. These findings delineate the molecular mechanism of quercetin in IUA treatment and present an effective strategy to overcome its pharmacokinetic barriers, underscoring the therapeutic potential of Que-Exo for preventing endometrial fibrosis.

papers.title: Natural products as selective estrogen receptor modulators in depression-related disorders: Balancing antidepressant efficacy and safety.
papers.authors: Chen R, Luo J, He K, Yang D, Zhao H
papers.abstract: Depression-related disorders remain major clinical challenges, and increasing evidence suggests that estrogen receptor (ER) signaling is involved in processes relevant to depression, including neuroinflammation, synaptic plasticity, neurotransmission, and stress regulation. Natural products and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas have attracted growing attention because of their multi-target regulatory effects on ER-related pathways. This narrative review summarizes ER-related pharmacological evidence of natural products and TCM preparations in depression-related disorders, with emphasis on flavonoids, stilbenes, lignans, and terpenoids. Evidence was interpreted according to depression relevance and the directness of ER involvement. Current findings suggest that ERα, ERβ, and G protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) are implicated in depression-related regulation through partially overlapping and context-dependent mechanisms, with their relative roles varying according to brain region, cell type, endocrine state, ligand properties, and exposure. Some natural products have been reported to exhibit SERM-like or context-dependent estrogenic activity; however, receptor-subtype selectivity and tissue-selective safety remain incompletely established. Across separate experimental studies, TCM formulas have been associated with ER-related signaling alterations together with modulation of 5-HT, BDNF, NLRP3, and neuroendocrine pathways, supporting mechanistic convergence rather than experimentally demonstrated synergy. Collectively, subtype- and context-dependent ER modulation represents a hypothesis-generating framework for evaluating natural product-based candidates in depression-related disorders, while currently available evidence does not establish selective ER modulation or clinically validated tissue-specific safety advantages.

papers.title: Targeting the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway by Xihuang Pill to restrict osteosarcoma progression: an integrated network pharmacology and in vivo/vitro study.
papers.authors: Hou C, Xie T, Wang J, Wang Z
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is an aggressive bone malignancy with limited treatment options. Xihuang Pill (XHP), a traditional Chinese medicine formulation, has shown anti-tumour activity, but its mechanisms in OS remain unclear. This study integrated UPLC-QTOF-MS, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation to identify the active components and therapeutic targets of XHP against OS. Network and survival analyses indicated that the PI3K/AKT pathway may be the key therapeutic axis. In vitro, XHP inhibited OS cell proliferation and migration, induced apoptosis, and caused cell cycle arrest in a dose- and time-dependent manner. In vivo, XHP suppressed xenograft tumour growth and improved physiological indicators in nude mice. RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry further confirmed that XHP exerted anti-OS effects by inhibiting PI3K/AKT signalling. These findings suggest that XHP may suppress OS progression through the PI3K/AKT pathway and has potential as a therapeutic candidate for OS.
